correctness.rationale: The iterates are palindromes and their 1 positions are even (base-3 digits in {0,2}); hence a nonzero even palindrome cannot exist, and the maximum zero run is L=3^(k-1). The proof constructs both distinct centered nonzero palindromes at every short odd length and the full C_k center at every long odd length. Together with zero powers, these give exactly 3^k distinct palindromes. The universal theorem that a length-N word has <=N distinct nonempty palindrome factors forces no further factors at any length and proves the explicit classification for all k. Independently written center expansion and canonical comparisons matched all lengths for k=1..7; finite tests are corroboration only.
residual_risks: Publisher text of Lü et al 2016 was partly accessible; an unindexed Sierpinski/Cantor full-text appendix could contain equivalent factors.

The original useful assertion is instead the exact length-by-length finite-factor spectrum with explicit representatives and cutoff. General palindromic complexity and palindromic decomposition lengths are not the same statement. Best-of-knowledge PASS; older Sierpinski-word tables could contain an equivalent classification.
